hero.title: X (Twitter) video length limit
hero.lead: On a free X account a video can be at most 2 minutes 20 seconds long and 512 MB. Premium raises that to 4 hours and 16 GB, though anything over 2 hours is served at 720p, and the Android app caps uploads at 10 minutes even with Premium. For most people the 2:20 is the wall — and the fix is a cut, not a smaller file.
qa.h2: X video limits at a glance
qa.after: The length limit is checked before the size limit ever matters: 2 minutes 20 of phone footage is well under 512 MB. So a free-account video that X refuses is almost always too long, not too large, and shrinking the file won't change the answer.
tool.h2: Trim your video to 2:20 or less
tool.lead: Drop the video below and drag the start and end handles over the preview until the line underneath reads 2:20 or less. The cut is exact to a tenth of a second and the result is a standard MP4, made on your own device — nothing is uploaded until you post it.
fit.h2: How long can a video on X be?
fit.caption: X video length limits
fit.r2.q: Up to 4 hours and 16 GB — over 2 hours it plays at 720p
fit.r4.len: Longer clips on a free account
fit.r4.q: Trim to 2:20, or post several clips in a thread
fit.after: These figures are checked against X's own help pages; the date they were last verified is at the top of this page. X changes them with its subscription tiers, so recheck before relying on the long-form limits.
over.h2: Too long for X? Cut it
over.p1: For a free account the only fix is length: trim the video to 2:20 or less, or split a longer piece into several clips and post them as a thread. Compressing changes the size, which was never the problem. Premium lifts the wall to 4 hours, but uploads from the Android app are still capped at 10 minutes — use the website or iOS for anything longer.
over.p2: Everything on this page runs locally in your browser — your video never leaves your device, and there is no account or watermark. If a file is genuinely near the 512 MB cap, the compressor brings it down while keeping the picture sharp.
faq.q1: How long can a video be on X without Premium?
faq.a1: 2 minutes 20 seconds, and up to 512 MB. The length is what stops most uploads; 2:20 of phone footage is far smaller than 512 MB.
faq.q2: How long can a video be with X Premium?
faq.a2: Up to 4 hours and 16 GB when uploading from the website or iOS. Videos over 2 hours are played back at 720p, and the Android app caps uploads at 10 minutes even for Premium subscribers.
faq.q3: Why does X reject my video when it's under 512 MB?
faq.a3: Because it's over 2 minutes 20 seconds. X checks length as well as size, and on a free account length is almost always the limit that fails. Trim it to 2:20 or less.
faq.a4: Hardly — the kept range is re-encoded at a high setting, and X recompresses uploads to its own settings anyway. The cut lands exactly where you place it, to a tenth of a second.
faq.q5: Is my video uploaded when I trim it here?
faq.a5: No. Compression runs in your browser on your own device — there is no server, no account and no watermark. The only place your video goes is where you post or send it yourself.
